title: Junebug Creek Rising
premise: Ulyana Zhou is three missed payments from losing Junebug Creek's beloved bakery when her charmingly infuriating regular, ferry mechanic Dev Okafor, offers to pose as her boyfriend for a family reunion that could unlock a loan from her estranged aunt. What starts as a transactional fake date turns devastatingly real over one weekend of shared lies, old wounds, and a storm that strands them together past the last ferry of the season. As Ulyana's café faces foreclosure and Dev's own buried secret — a brother he abandoned back home — surfaces, they must decide whether loyalty to the people who raised them matters more than the truths that could set them free. In the end, Ulyana saves the bakery by selling her aunt the recipes she swore she'd never share, Dev boards the first spring ferry to make things right with his brother, and Ulyana chooses to wait — because some people are worth the last train, the last ferry, and every season after.
about_author: Ansel Eastwick is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade writing love stories on the backs of order tickets in small coastal towns. They live somewhere between two ferry terminals and believe every good romance deserves at least one storm.

chapters.title: Three Payments from Gone
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She opens Junebug Creek Bakery before dawn, counts the foreclosure notice twice, and serves Dev his usual cardamom buns while hiding how bad things are. Emotional beat: quiet desperation masked as competence, and the first flicker that Dev sees through her.

chapters.title: The Regular Who Lingers
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. He fixes the bakery's ancient oven for free, lingering past closing, and learns from the town gossip that Ulyana's family reunion is in ten days — and that her aunt holds the purse strings to everything. Emotional beat: longing disguised as helpfulness.

chapters.title: An Offer Over Cold Coffee
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Dev proposes a fake relationship: he'll attend the reunion as her boyfriend if she teaches him to bake his late mother's honey cake. She refuses, pride intact, then finds the second foreclosure notice taped to her door. Emotional beat: the sting of needing help.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. They negotiate rules over cold coffee — no real feelings, no questions about his past, one weekend only. Ulyana agrees, telling herself it's strictly business. Emotional beat: the delicious tension of a deal both parties already want to break.

chapters.title: Lessons in Honey and Flour
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Their first baking lesson dissolves into flour fights and a near-kiss over the honey cake batter. Dev deflects a question about his family so smoothly it frightens her. Emotional beat: warmth creeping past the boundaries they drew.

chapters.title: The Ferry at Dusk
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. He walks Ulyana to the ferry dock and confesses, in fragments, that he hasn't been home in six years. She doesn't push, and the not-pushing feels more intimate than anything they've rehearsed. Emotional beat: vulnerability traded like contraband.

chapters.title: Arriving as a Lie
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. They arrive at the Zhou family estate on Junebug Creek's upper inlet, and Ulyana's mother clocks the hand-holding instantly — with suspicious delight. Her aunt Marguerite watches Dev like an auditor. Emotional beat: performing a love that keeps accidentally becoming real.

chapters.title: Aunt Marguerite's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Over dinner, Marguerite interrogates him about finances and intentions, and Dev realizes Ulyana never told her family about the foreclosure. He covers for her, lying beautifully, and hates how good it feels. Emotional beat: protective instinct masquerading as acting.

chapters.title: The Reunion Games
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A chaotic family field day forces them onto the same tug-of-war team; her cousins adopt Dev completely, and Ulyana watches him become part of something he clearly aches for. Emotional beat: found family forming in real time, and the guilt of knowing it's built on a lie.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The weather service issues a gale warning; the last ferry of the season leaves at noon tomorrow, and after that, nothing crosses the creek for months. Marguerite hints the loan depends on whether Dev 'stays the winter.' Emotional beat: the clock starts ticking on everything.

chapters.title: Dessert and the Truth Adjacent
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana serves her grandmother's plum tart and, swept up in the evening, nearly tells Marguerite the truth — until Dev's hand finds hers under the table. Later, on the porch, they argue about who's protecting whom. Emotional beat: the fake date feels too real by dessert, and both know it.

chapters.title: The Storm Hits
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The gale lands early, knocking out power and flooding the boathouse. Dev and Ulyana work side by side hauling her aunt's boats clear, soaked and laughing, until a wave nearly takes him and she pulls him back. Emotional beat: adrenaline stripping away every pretense.

chapters.title: Stranded Past the Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The storm cancels the last ferry of the season. Dev is stuck at the estate for the winter, and the fake-boyfriend arrangement collapses into something neither of them can name. They fall asleep on the parlor floor by firelight, hands barely touching. Emotional beat: the terrifying freedom of having no exit plan.

chapters.title: Winter in a Stranger's House
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev settles into the estate, fixing what the storm broke, and grows close to Ulyana's grandmother, who shares stories about Ulyana's late father. Dev recognizes the shape of grief he's been running from. Emotional beat: belonging arriving through the back door.

chapters.title: The Brother on the Phone
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana accidentally overhears Dev on a crackling call — a brother named Sam, a debt of shame, a promise Dev keeps breaking. She says nothing, but the secrecy curdles. Emotional beat: loyalty to his privacy warring with the hunger for truth.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Offer
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Marguerite offers Ulyana the loan — but only if she sells the bakery building and works under Marguerite's brand. Ulyana refuses, and Dev watches her choose pride over survival, furious and awed. Emotional beat: the price of survival made brutally concrete.

chapters.title: The Fight at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana confronts Dev about Sam; he explodes, revealing he left home after their father's death and never forgave himself. She tells him secrets kept 'to protect people' are just lies with better manners. Emotional beat: the loyalty-versus-truth theme detonating between them.

chapters.title: The Empty Kitchen
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev leaves before dawn, walking to the frozen dock with no ferry to catch, just distance to put between them. Ulyana finds his half-finished honey cake cooling on her counter and a note: 'You deserve someone who stays.' Emotional beat: the black moment — love abandoned to protect it.

chapters.title: Recipes as Collateral
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Facing final foreclosure, Ulyana makes her own bargain: she sells Marguerite her family's recipe book — not the building — in exchange for the loan, keeping the café and losing a piece of her inheritance. Her grandmother, revealing she knew all along, blesses the trade. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid knowingly, with grace.

chapters.title: The Letter from Sam
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev finally calls his brother; Sam isn't angry, he's been waiting six years for Dev to come home. Dev buys a bus ticket and writes Ulyana a letter he doesn't send, then sends it anyway from the first town with a mailbox. Emotional beat: choosing truth over the comfort of exile.

chapters.title: First Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Spring arrives; the first ferry of the season crosses Junebug Creek, and Ulyana, flour-dusted, watches it dock without letting herself hope. Dev steps off with Sam beside him, holding the unsent letter and a jar of his mother's honey. Emotional beat: the return, and the terror of hoping anyway.

chapters.title: Someone Who Stays
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Dev asks for nothing except a chance to be the man who stays; Ulyana hands him an apron instead of an answer, which is her answer. The bakery reopens with Sam at the register and Marguerite at a corner table. Emotional beat: found family sealed, second chances finally well-timed.
